title: SRE — Inference Serving: interview rubric and practical exercises
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a reproducible interview loop, scoring rubric, and practical exercises for hiring Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) who will own Redwood's inference serving runtime. Goal: hire candidates who can reliably operate low-latency, high-throughput model serving, diagnose production regressions, and contribute to platform optimizations (batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs).

Context / constraints:
- Most hires will be remote-first engineers who must move quickly from local repros to cluster-level fixes.
- The role spans on-call incident response, performance tuning (latency/tokens/sec), and small-to-medium feature work.
- We intentionally bias for system-level thinking and pragmatic debugging over algorithmic-only skill.
body_2:
Interview loop (recommended):
1) Recruiter screen (30m): culture, background, relocation/benefits logistics.
2) Technical phone (45m): systems debugging, short coding exercise (read/write small Go/Python snippet).
3) Onsite (4h, remote-friendly sequence or two half-days):
   - 60m System design: architecture of a high-throughput inference path (routing, batching, cache).
   - 45m Live debugging lab: given traces/metrics, find root cause of a regression.
   - 45m Coding: microservice-level change (idempotent request handler, KV cache invalidation).
   - 30m Incident simulation (tabletop): communicate triage steps to PM/engineer stakeholders.
   - 30m Behavioral: ownership, postmortems, working with model teams.

Scoring rubric (1–5 scale per axis, interviewer records bullet evidence):
- System Design (1–5): clarity of tradeoffs (latency vs throughput, consistency vs eventual correctness), awareness of model-specific needs (kv cache warmup, prefix caching).
- Debugging & Observability (1–5): reads traces/metrics, forms hypothesis, proposes testable remediation (e.g., disable batching, repro with shorter seq).
- Idiomatic Code & Testing (1–5): code quality, defensive checks, unit-testable design, small PR hygiene.
- Incident Response & Communication (1–5): prioritization under pressure, runbook usage, stakeholder updates.
- Production Judgement / Cost Awareness (1–5): ability to reason about batch sizing, GPU utilization, and cost tradeoffs.
- Ownership & Collaboration (1–5): postmortem framing, follow-through plan, cross-team coordination.

Minimum bar: overall average >= 3.5 with no critical score of 1 in Debugging or Incident Response. Hiring manager may raise bar for senior levels.

Live debugging lab (design):
- Candidate receives: a synthetic timeline (API latency spike for a specific model at 02:18 UTC), excerpts from request traces, p95/p99 CPU/GPU utilization, and recent deploy PR IDs.
- They have 30–45 minutes to:
  * Identify the likeliest root cause (e.g., caching eviction, quantized model mismatch, kernel fallback) and evidence supporting it.
  * Propose and sketch two remediation paths: quick mitigations (roll back, pin model version, disable dynamic batching) and medium-term fixes (improved knobging, telemetry).
  * Write the exact commands/queries they'd run (kubectl logs grep, tracing span filters, DB queries) and which metrics to watch post-fix.

Sample debugging prompts (pick 1):
- p99 latency for chat-gen doubled after a change that updated model weights + quantization profile. Telemetry shows GPU memcpy spikes and smaller effective batch size. Candidate should reason about kernel selection and quantization fallback.
- A small % of requests start returning truncated outputs; logs show increased LRU evictions in the prefix cache during sustained load. Candidate should map eviction policies to latency and quality tradeoffs.

Coding exercise (onsite):
- Implement a small HTTP handler that receives batched inference requests, performs safe deduplication of identical prefix requests, and emits tracing spans for each request. Languages: Go or Python (candidate choice). Focus evaluation: correctness, idempotency, test sketch, edge cases (timeouts, partial failures).

Take-home exercise (optional for senior hires):
- 48-hour take-home: given a toy serving runtime repo (link provided), add a configurable prefix cache with TTL and an end-to-end unit/integration test that demonstrates improved throughput for a synthetic load. Evaluate for code design, test coverage, and performance reasoning.

Red flags (immediate reject notes):
- No structured approach to debugging (no hypothesis, or flails through metrics).
- Suggests only costly, long-term changes as immediate mitigations (e.g., rewrite executor) without safety nets.
- Poor written communication in PR-style notes.

Green flags (pass/strength notes):
- Reproduces failures locally with small load generators and proposes low-risk rollbacks.
- Explains batching tradeoffs in terms of cost-per-token and queueing latency.
- Shows familiarity with GPU-local problems (kernel fallbacks, memcpy, small-batch inefficiency).

Interviewer choreography & roles (onsite):
- System design: senior eng (Marco Ruiz) — evaluate architecture mental models.
- Debugging lab: SRE hire loop lead (Aisha Patel) — observe hypothesis formation.
- Coding: platform engineer (Priya Desai) — the code authoring and test framing.
- Incident tabletop: product/PM or solutions engineer — evaluate communication.

Feedback capture template (one line bullets + score fields for each axis):
- Summary: "Hire / No hire / Strong hire" + 2-line rationale.
- Evidence bullets (3): candidate said X which indicates Y.
- Improvements suggested (if any).

First-30-days practical onramp (People Ops + Hiring manager checklist):
- Pre-day-1: create infra access, cloud IAM perms, Slack invites (#serving-runtime, #oncall), JIRA rights.
- Day 1–3: read runbooks, onboarding run of bootstrapped local dev (repo link), shadow a runbook-driven incident.
- Week 1: pair on a low-risk perf-tuning ticket (assign to mentor), complete a micro-PR (observability or a test).
- Week 2–4: own a small on-call rotation slot with mentor shadow, write first postmortem template for a simulated outage, advocate one perf knob change with data.

Onboarding artifacts to attach for new hire:
- Serving runtime quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/quickstart
- Runbooks: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Runbooks
- Observability dashboards: grafana/redwood/serving-runtime (request access in #serving-runtime)

Notes for hiring manager and interviewers:
- Be explicit about level expectations: senior SRE expected to propose medium-term architectural fixes; staff should demonstrate cross-team influence.
- Use rubric as a conversation starter; capture concrete evidence not impressions.
- For remote candidates, provide a short local repro (docker-compose) ahead of the debug session so network/setup time is minimized.

Appendix: example candidate prompt (copy/paste into interview instructions)
- "At 02:18 UTC, p99 latency for 'chat-generate-v2' rose from 320ms to 820ms. Recent deploy notes show: PR#987 changed the quantization profile. CPU and GPU metrics show a spike in GPU memcpy time and a drop in effective batch size. You have 35 minutes to investigate, choose a mitigation, and list commands you'd run. Write the three top data points you'd look at and the rollback steps if your mitigation fails."
